# Implement version read + dimmed right-aligned header display

## Summary
Read the plugin version at runtime from `packages/herdr/package.json` and render it as a dimmed, right-aligned `v<version>` suffix in the work item selection list header, without disturbing the left-aligned title.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A runtime helper reads the plugin version from `packages/herdr/package.json` (JSON parse via `readFileSync`, following the `shortcut-config.ts` pattern); when the file is missing or unparseable it falls back gracefully (e.g. `'?'` or omit) without throwing.
- The list-mode header renders `v<version>` right-aligned to `cols` (visible-width padding computed with ANSI codes stripped before padding), dimmed via `ANSI.dim`, matching the `[auto-refresh on]` treatment; the left-aligned `Work Items — N item(s)` title is unchanged.
- The version is read at runtime from the manifest, not hardcoded in the renderer (stays in sync with the manifest version).
- On narrow panes where the suffix would overlap the title, the suffix is dropped or truncated (guard on `cols`) — no layout breakage, no overflow beyond the pane width.
- Full project test suite passes with the new changes, including the header version tests (F1).

## Minimal Implementation
- Add a small version-read helper in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` (or a sibling module) using the `readFileSync`/`dirname` pattern from `shortcut-config.ts`, with a safe fallback.
- In the list-mode header renderer (near line ~1585): compute the header's visible width, pad to `cols`, and append the dimmed `v<version>` suffix right-aligned; reuse `truncateLine`/visible-length logic; guard on `cols` for narrow panes.
- Keep the renderer testable via the existing `readFile`-style injection seam where practical.

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: header version rendering tests (F1) — test-first ordering.

## Deliverables
- Updated `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`; version helper; no change to `packages/herdr/package.json` (version source only).

# Extract worklist constants, types and layout

**Parent:** WL-0MVGKGD2Y0038S6B. **Phase:** 1 of 7 extraction slices (leaf modules).

## Target outcome

The three leaf modules of the split exist, carry the module-level doc comments
required by parent AC6, and `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` re-exports them from
its barrel position — no consumer or test change required.

## Scope (measured line ranges on the current `dev` tree)

| New module | Contents (current `worklist.ts` lines) | Est. size |
|---|---|---|
| `worklist.constants.ts` | Constants (164–224): `SHIP_IT_COMMAND`, `STAGES`/`Stage`, `STAGE_MAP`, `PRIORITY_MAP`, `STAGE_COLORS`; `ANSI` (345–368); mouse timing `DOUBLE_CLICK_WINDOW_MS`, `DRAG_THRESHOLD_CELLS` (3558–3592); any tooltip/chord tuning constants | ~170 |

| `worklist.layout.ts` | `MIN_META_SHARE`, `MAX_META_SHARE`, `computeMetadataPanelHeight`, `computeDynamicLayout` (226–316), `getTermSize` (327–344) | ~130 |

`worklist.types.ts` **must be a leaf**: type-only declarations, no imports from
any other `worklist.*` module (parent AC4 — this is what keeps later modules
cycle-free).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `worklist.constants.ts`, `worklist.types.ts` and `worklist.layout.ts` exist,
   each ≤1,000 lines, each opening with a doc comment stating its single
   responsibility (AC6).
2. Provenance comments move with their code: the `// ── Constants ──`,
   `// ── /wl <stage> argument map (WL-0MSDT8X1V003206G) ──`,
   `// ── /wl --priority <priority> map (WL-0MSKC8T46006999S) ──`,
   `// ── Metadata panel sizing ──`, `// ── Terminal helpers ──` banners and all
   inline work-item ids survive verbatim in the destination modules.
3. `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` re-exports the symbols in this slice that
   consumers actually use — `ANSI`, `SHIP_IT_COMMAND`, `STAGES`, `Stage`,
   `TermSize`, `getTermSize`, `computeMetadataPanelHeight`,
   `computeDynamicLayout`, `DOUBLE_CLICK_WINDOW_MS`, `DRAG_THRESHOLD_CELLS`,
   `DisplayRow`, `DisplayHeadingRow`, `ChordState`, `ParsedMouseEvent`,
   `MouseDragState`, `MouseClickState`, `MouseAction`. **Internal** (declared in
   the new modules, exported from them for sibling use, but *not* re-exported by
   the barrel, because no external consumer imports them): `KeyAction`,
   `HelpIconRow`, `NoteEditAction`, `ReviewQueueBannerState`, `PodcastNotice`,
   `ExecuteResult`, `PodcastTargetResolution`, `ViewMode`, `MIN_META_SHARE`,
   `MAX_META_SHARE`.
   *(Plan-time correction, 2026-10-30: the guarded symbol set is re-derived
from the live import scan — 66 symbols are imported by the 36 consumer
files. Every symbol listed as internal below is imported by no external
consumer, so parent AC2 requires it to stay module-private.)*
4. `worklist.split-guard.test.ts` is green: every baseline/consumer symbol still
   exported from `./worklist.js`, no worklist module imports the barrel at
   runtime, no new cycle, all modules ≤1,000 lines (AC4, AC1, AC2).
5. `tsc --noEmit` (or `npm run build` in `packages/herdr`) succeeds and the full
   `packages/herdr` suite passes with **no test-file changes** (AC3, AC9).
6. Documentation that names these symbols is updated to the new module paths:
   `packages/herdr/README.md` (module-layout block around line 2345 and the
   `ANSI`/colour references), `docs/COLOUR-MAPPING.md` (line 77) if the
   `formatItemLine` reference needs the new home (deferred there if format has
   not moved yet — record the deferral in a comment).
7. **Behaviour-preserving, move-only refactor.** No functional or logic change,
   no renames of public symbols, no behavioural diffs. No test file is modified —
   not its import paths, fixtures or assertions — and all 24 `worklist*.test.ts`
   suites (15,988 lines) plus the whole `packages/herdr` suite pass unchanged.
   → Owned by this slice: no test file is modified and the `packages/herdr` suite is green.
8. **No new circular imports.** Extracted modules import only from concrete
   sibling modules, never from the `worklist.js` barrel or from `index.ts`; the
   existing `worklist → fetcher/visibility/…` edge direction is preserved and no
   new cycle is introduced.
   → Owned by this slice: the guard's cycle gate reports no new circular import.
9. **Responsibility documented per module.** Each new module carries a
   module-level doc comment stating its single responsibility, and existing
   provenance comments (work-item ids, section banners such as
   `// ── Mouse / touch input (WL-0MSGHM5BQ0096BNJ) ──`) move with their code so
   traceability is preserved.
   → Owned by this slice: each module created here carries a responsibility doc comment and the moved provenance banners/comments are verbatim.

# Downtime leader cannot see a worklog root with no running herdr instance

The downtime leader discovers candidates only from live herdr instance offers plus its own backlog, so a worklog root with dispatchable work but no running instance is invisible. This item adds explicit **registered-root discovery** (option O1) so the leader sweeps configured roots under the same sequential safety gates, and makes the peer-offer predicate liveness-aware.

# Problem Statement

The downtime leader's candidate universe is derived exclusively from live herdr instances that write coordination entries. A worklog root with dispatchable work but no running herdr instance is invisible to the dispatcher, meaning work from that root can never be dispatched — even when the leader has idle capacity and the work satisfies every safety gate.

# Users

- **Operator running multiple worklog roots on one machine**: Needs all roots with dispatchable work to be discoverable and served by the downtime leader, regardless of whether a herdr instance is currently running in each root.
- **Downtime leader (herdr instance)**: Needs a reliable mechanism to discover candidate roots beyond the offer list and its own backlog.

# Existing State

The leader discovers candidates through two paths:
1. **The offer list** (`downtime-coordination.json`): Machine-wide file containing one entry per running instance, each offering one item.
2. **Own-backlog fallback** (`runCoordinationCheckIn` → `computeMostImportantItem`): Only scoped to `opts.cwd` — the leader's own root.

A root without a running instance writes no coordination entry, so the leader has zero visibility into it. The empty-leader hand-off (WL-0MVP7QHUB003ZA2A) hands off to a peer, but there is no peer in a root with no instance.

# Options Evaluated (at intake)

| Option | Description | Pros | Cons | Verdict |
|--------|-------------|------|------|---------|
| **O1 — Registered roots** | Explicit config list (`downtimeWorklogRoots` array in settings), or discovery by scanning a parent directory for `.worklog/worklog.db`. Leader sweeps registered roots round-robin via `getHerdrListHead` and applies the same sequential filter chain. | Clean separation of concerns; explicit and predictable; fails-safe (empty config = current behaviour); aligns with AC6; no runtime coupling to running instances | Requires config management; needs a new settings field with validation | **RECOMMENDED** |
| **O2 — Per-root offers from single instance** | One instance offers on behalf of a set of roots, writing multiple entries to the coordination file. | Cheaper than O1 (no config file); reuses coordination infrastructure | Reintroduces "who offers which root" ownership complexity; a single instance failure takes down multiple roots | NOT RECOMMENDED |
| **O3 — Heartbeat registry** | Instances publish liveness per root so the leader distinguishes "no instance" from "offered nothing". | Could address the stale-entry issue too | Over-engineered; adds infrastructure; doesn't directly solve root discovery; overlaps with existing stale-entry problem | NOT RECOMMENDED (defer to separate work) |

# Recommendation

**Adopt O1 — Registered roots** with a `downtimeWorklogRoots: string[]` settings field (paths to `.worklog` directories). The leader sweeps registered roots in round-robin order using `getHerdrListHead(root, window)`, then applies the same sequential filter chain as the offer path. The retired `downtime-round-robin-by-root.ts` cursor machinery can be reused.

**Stale coordination entries (AC7):** Make `hasPeerOffer` liveness-aware (check `lastUpdated` against `DEFAULT_DOWNTIME_MARKER_STALE_WINDOW_MS`) rather than reinstating entry expiry. This is conservative: stale entries are treated as absent peers, making the leader *more* willing to sweep rather than less. Decision recorded per AC7.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1**: A root with dispatchable work but no running herdr instance is reachable by the leader, and work from it is dispatched. Verified on ContextHub (9 dispatchable items, 0 offers → now dispatchable).
- **AC2**: A sweep must not bypass any existing safety gate — assignee hold, producer-review, code-freeze, freshness, caps, slot minimums, in-flight, review-queue. Gates remain sequential filters.
- **AC3**: The canonical ranking contract is preserved: a sweep is a bounded window over registered roots using the same `getHerdrListHead` path, never a second ranking.
- **AC4**: Fairness: no single root can monopolise the leader (bounded per-root share or round-robin cursor), demonstrated by a multi-root test with two roots each holding dispatchable work.
- **AC5**: Fail-open: an unreadable/missing root in the registry is skipped without a strike, and never crashes the tick.
- **AC6**: Fail-safe: an empty or unresolvable registry leaves today's behaviour byte-for-byte unchanged (only offers + own-backlog).
- **AC7**: `hasPeerOffer` is made liveness-aware (rejects entries older than `DEFAULT_DOWNTIME_MARKER_STALE_WINDOW_MS`), and the decision is recorded in code comments and docs. Entry expiry remains a no-op.
- **AC8**: `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` documents the root-discovery model (registered roots) and how it composes with the offer list.
- **AC9**: Testing/validation: unit tests cover the registered-root sweep (multi-root fairness, fail-open, fail-safe, gate preservation) and `hasPeerOffer` liveness; existing downtime-worker and coordination suites remain green.
- **AC10**: All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `packages/herdr/README.md`, and `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` (`CHANGELOG.md` is managed by the ship skill and excluded).
- **AC11**: Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Must not reinstate the unconditional non-critical window widening superseded by WL-0MUNS8X97007C9H9.
- Must not require a running pane per root (that is the bug being fixed).
- Config schema additions need clamping/validation consistent with `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts`.
- Round-robin cursor machinery in `downtime-round-robin-by-root.ts` is retired but functional — reuse preferred over rewrite.
- Stale coordination entry expiry remains a deliberate no-op; only `hasPeerOffer` predicate changes.

# Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.coordination-leader.ts` — Leader dispatch loop; add registered-root sweep path
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.coordination.ts` — `computeMostImportantItem`; adapt for external roots
- `packages/herdr/src/coordination.ts` — `hasPeerOffer` predicate; add liveness check
- `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts` — New `downtimeWorklogRoots` setting with validation
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-round-robin-by-root.ts` — Reuse cursor for round-robin over roots
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — Update to document root-discovery model

# Related Work

- **WL-0MVR8EXR6009F05V** (epic) — Downtime dispatcher audit: the epic that this item was discovered-from. Completed. Its AC2 ContextHub leg remains unmet specifically because this root-registry cause was out of scope.
- **WL-0MVP7QHUB003ZA2A** — Empty-leader hand-off: peer stepping down. Not directly related — the hand-off assumes a peer exists, which doesn't solve the "no instance in root" case.
- **WL-0MSORQ1RG005DGUS** — Audit tier two-slot requirement. The safety gates this item must preserve.
- **WL-0MTMPIQBE001J41P** — Stale coordination entry pruning (deliberate no-op). Directly related to AC7.
- **WL-0MTJDX4M4007YH5U** — Global round-robin cursor module (`downtime-round-robin-by-root`). The retired-but-functional cursor machinery to reuse for root-level round-robin (AC4).
- **WL-0MST3OJ8S0001ROL** — Leader election with shared coordination file. The coordination/offer architecture this change must compose with.
- **WL-0MW1VINII003IL7R** — Elected leader has no coordination entry (invisible dispatching instance). Related coordination-file visibility work.
- **WL-0MUNS8X97007C9H9** — Superseded unconditional non-critical window widening. Constraint: must not reinstate.

# Existing State

The current dispatcher candidate universe is:
```
candidates = offerList ∪ { ownBacklogHead(opts.cwd) }
```
The leader never scans beyond its own root and the offer file. No root discovery mechanism exists.

# Desired Change

```
candidates = offerList ∪ sweepRegisteredRoots() ∪ { ownBacklogHead(opts.cwd) }
```
Where `sweepRegisteredRoots()` iterates a registered roots list in round-robin order, applying `getHerdrListHead` and the full sequential filter chain for each root.

# Decisions (recorded)

- **D1 (root discovery)**: **O1 — Registered roots** (producer-confirmed 2026-11-06): explicit `downtimeWorklogRoots` config list; leader sweeps registered roots round-robin via `getHerdrListHead` under the same sequential gates.
- **D2 (AC7 stale entries)**: **Liveness-aware `hasPeerOffer`** (producer-confirmed 2026-11-06): entries older than `DEFAULT_DOWNTIME_MARKER_STALE_WINDOW_MS` count as absent peers; `pruneStaleEntries` remains a deliberate no-op. This is the more conservative approach — it never makes the leader *less* willing to sweep (the existing "conservative, never starvation" intent is preserved).

# Risks & Assumptions

- **Scope creep risk**: The stale-entry liveness check (AC7) is scoped to `hasPeerOffer` only. Heartbeat expiry, peer-liveness broadcasts, or a separate heartbeat registry are out of scope and should be tracked as follow-up items.
- **Config management risk**: A `downtimeWorklogRoots` array adds a new configuration surface. If the array is large, parsing and validation should be bounded. Risk mitigated: TypeScript array of strings with length clamp.
- **A1**: The `downtimeWorklogRoots` setting is additive — empty or absent array falls through to today's offer-only + own-backlog behaviour (AC6 satisfied).
- **A2**: Round-robin cursor from `downtime-round-robin-by-root.ts` can be reused as-is for root-level iteration (not item-level).
- **A3**: The sequential filter chain (gates.ts) works generically over `DowntimeHerdrItem` regardless of root source — no gate changes needed.
- **Assumption**: No root should appear in the registry that is not a valid worklog root with a `.worklog/worklog.db`.
- **Failure mode**: If a registered root's `.worklog/` directory is a symlink to an unexpected location, the leader could dispatch into the wrong workspace. Mitigation: validate root paths at config load time.

# Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q: "Which option should we pursue for root discovery?" — Answer (intake agent, based on code inspection): O1 — Registered roots. Rationale: cleanest separation of concerns, explicit, fails-safe, aligns with AC6, reuses existing cursor machinery (`downtime-round-robin-by-root.ts`). O2 reintroduces ownership complexity; O3 is over-engineered for this problem. Source: intake evaluation — code inspection of `downtime-worker.coordination-leader.ts`, `coordination.ts`, `settings.ts`. **Final accepted answer (producer, 2026-11-06): O1 confirmed.**
- Q: "How should stale coordination entries be handled?" — Answer (intake agent): Make `hasPeerOffer` liveness-aware (check `lastUpdated` against `DEFAULT_DOWNTIME_MARKER_STALE_WINDOW_MS`). Do not reinstate entry expiry (remains a deliberate no-op). Source: intake evaluation — preserves the existing conservative intent without re-enabling expiry-based churn. **Final accepted answer (producer, 2026-11-06): Option A confirmed — liveness-aware `hasPeerOffer`, expiry stays a no-op.**
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MTJDX4M4007YH5U** – Implement: global round-robin cursor module (downtime-round-robin-by-root) (completed)
- **WL-0MTJDPIZP007CA79** – Test: global round-robin cursor module (downtime-round-robin-by-root) (completed)
- **WL-0MST3OJ8S0001ROL** – Refactor Downtime Dispatcher: leader election with shared coordination file (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: 0mst3oj8s0001rol, 0mtmpiqbe001j41p, 0muns8x97007c9h9, 0mvp7qhub003za2a, 0mw1vinii003il7r (+343 more)
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: 0msorq1rg005dgus, 0mst3oj8s0001rol, 0mtmpiqbe001j41p, 0muns8x97007c9h9, absent (+330 more)
- `CLI.md` — matched: absent, ac2, add, additive, adds (+262 more)

## Impact

Worklog roots registered via `downtimeWorklogRoots` are now swept by the downtime leader even with no herdr instance running in them, and a dead peer's stale coordination entry no longer blocks the leader from picking up that work — so multi-root operators no longer have to keep a pane open per root for its backlog to be dispatched.

# Extract shared data-file push preamble helper

Refactor child of WL-0MVPUCVXL0099TND (*Deduplicate the worktree/push preamble
shared by `gitPushDataFileToBranch` and `rewriteAndForcePushDataFile`). Its
sibling *Pin push-path policy divergence with tests* lands the behavioural tests
first; this child performs the dedupe and must leave those tests untouched and
green.

## Why

`gitPushDataFileToBranch` (incremental) and `rewriteAndForcePushDataFile`
(rewrite) in `src/sync/push.ts` each carry a near-identical preamble:

1. cross-project guard (`assertDataFileInCwdRepo`)
2. `refs/heads/` + `refs/tags/` safety guard
3. `git rev-parse --git-dir`
4. repo-root / repo-relative-path resolution (`getRepoRoot`,
   `getRepoRelativePath`, `path.resolve`)
5. data-file existence check
6. `withTempWorktree(...)`
7. `ensureDir` + `copyFileSync`
8. `git add -f`
9. `git diff --cached`
10. `git commit`

A fix to any one of those steps must currently be made twice and can silently
drift.

## Desired change

One **private** helper in `src/sync/push.ts` (working name
`withDataFileInTempWorktree`) owns the preamble and delegates the
mode-specific tail to a callback:

- **Guard + resolve:** `assertDataFileInCwdRepo`, the refs rejection,
  `git rev-parse --git-dir`, `getRepoRoot()` / `getRepoRelativePath()` /
  `path.resolve()`, and the existence check.
- **Materialise:** `withTempWorktree(repoRootPath, target, …, { forceOrphan })`,
  `ensureDir` + `copyFileSync`, `add -f`, `diff --cached`.
- **Commit**, then invoke the caller's `run(worktreePath, relativePath, …)` so
  each caller performs only its own push and post-push bookkeeping.

The four documented behavioural differences must stay **explicit options**, not
collapsed:

- `emptyStage: 'skip' | 'throw'` — `'skip'` resolves as a no-op **without**
  invoking the callback; `'throw'` raises the existing
  `Nothing staged for the rewrite; aborting to avoid an empty ref` message.
- `missingFile: 'skip' | 'throw'` — `'skip'` returns silently; `'throw'` raises
  `Worklog data file not found: <path>`.
- `forceOrphan: boolean` — `true` only for the rewrite path.
- `skipPrePushHint: boolean` — `true` only for the incremental path, so both
  guard messages stay byte-identical to today.

The incremental path's foreign-tracked-file cleanup (`listTrackedFiles` +
`git rm` + `git clean -fdx`) stays in `gitPushDataFileToBranch`'s callback — it
is mode-specific, not preamble.

Both public functions then reduce to: resolve options → call the helper →
mode-specific push. The rewrite path additionally updates
`refs/worklog/remotes/<remote>/<branch>` and returns the new tip SHA.

## Constraints

- Pure refactor: no signature change, no behavioural change, no error-message
  change.
- No consumer edits; the `./sync.js` barrel surface is unchanged.
- The helper stays private to `src/sync/push.ts`; `src/sync/worktree.ts` stays a
  data-file-agnostic lifecycle layer and does not learn about data files.
- No scope creep into the duplicate read-side preamble in `src/sync/remote.ts`
  (record it as a separate follow-up if it is worth doing).
- Agent test runs go through `/skill:test` only.

## Risks to keep pinned

- **Empty-stage drift (highest risk).** A single policy applied to both paths
  would either publish nothing while reporting success (rewrite) or turn a
  routine no-change sync into an error (incremental). The sibling's
  negative-proof tests fail if this happens.
- **Guard-message merge.** Collapsing the two messages would drop the
  `Use WORKLOG_SKIP_PRE_PUSH=1` hint from the incremental path (or add it where
  it does not belong). The hint is an explicit parameter; the exact-text test
  pins it.
- **Lost `forceOrphan`.** If the helper does not thread `{ forceOrphan: true }`
  through to `withTempWorktree`, the rewrite path fetches the polluted ref
  again — the exact bug the earlier split fixed.
- **Return-type widening.** The rewrite path needs a value from inside the
  callback (tip SHA) while the skip policy produces nothing. The helper's
  generic return must stay honest so the rewrite caller cannot silently drop
  the SHA.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Single shared preamble.** One new private helper (e.g. `withDataFileInTempWorktree`) in `src/sync/push.ts` contains the cross-project guard, the refs safety guard, `git rev-parse --git-dir`, the repo-root/relative-path resolution, the existence check, and the `withTempWorktree` + copy + `add -f` + `diff --cached` + commit sequence; both `gitPushDataFileToBranch` and `rewriteAndForcePushDataFile` are implemented on top of it. Each of those steps appears exactly once in the file (inspection / duplicate-block assertion), and `src/sync/push.ts` gets shorter.
  - The helper owns: `assertDataFileInCwdRepo`, the refs safety guard, `git rev-parse --git-dir`, `getRepoRoot`/`getRepoRelativePath`/`path.resolve`, the existence check, `withTempWorktree` + `ensureDir` + `copyFileSync` + `add -f` + `diff --cached` + `commit`.
  - The four documented differences stay explicit options: `emptyStage: 'skip' | 'throw'`, `missingFile: 'skip' | 'throw'`, `forceOrphan` (rewrite only), `skipPrePushHint` (incremental only).

# Redirect post-push verification full-suite runs to a pinned isolated worktree

## Problem Statement

A full-suite run executed from the main checkout during post-push verification
can race with a sibling `implement.py finish` fast-forwarding the main
checkout's local `dev` (`git merge --ff-only`), swapping source files mid-run
and producing phantom failures (WL-0MVSLXT79008D4X6 evidence: 4 failures in
`tests/herdr/send-to-pi.test.ts` / `tests/herdr/settings.test.ts` at
1abe9618; identical tree green in an isolated worktree minutes earlier).

## Goal (User Story)

As an AI agent running `implement.py finish`, I want post-push verification and
audit cache-miss full-suite runs to execute in an isolated worktree pinned to
the pushed commit — never live in the main checkout — so a sibling finish
fast-forwarding `dev` cannot swap the files a suite is reading.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Mitigate the race:** the post-push verification path is updated so that
   full-suite runs execute in an isolated worktree against a pinned commit,
   and the cache entry is grafted into the main checkout — not run live in
   the main checkout where a sibling finish can fast-forward `dev` mid-run.
2. The post-push verification path (and the audit skill F3 cache-miss
   auto-execution path) resolves an isolated worktree for the commit being
   verified and executes the full suite there — not in the live main checkout
   where a sibling `finish` can fast-forward `dev` mid-run.
3. The fresh cache entry produced by the isolated-worktree run is grafted into
   the main checkout's `.worklog/cache` before/mirroring the pre-push hook's
   `mirror_suite_cache` semantics (never overwrites an existing entry), so
   read-only post-push verification and audits serve the grafted entry.
4. The mitigation is minimal and localised: document + redirect test execution
   to worktrees; it does not rewrite the post-push verification pipeline or
   change verdict semantics (`green`/`red`/`missing`/`not_applicable`).
5. The single-owner main-checkout flock lock (WL-0MVPE2DA7007WF84) and the
   main-checkout guard (WL-0MVPE2BY9001CR9O) remain intact; finish refuses
   loudly rather than masking a real failure.
6. The full project test suite passes with the change.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `phase_finish()` read-only
  verification step and Step-6 main-checkout dev fast-forward
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_run_tests_via_test_skill` /
  F3 auto-execution (`run_cached(..., cwd=per_audit_root)`)
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`, `skill/test_cache.py` — suite execution
  and cache
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — guidance to match

## Constraints

- Must not break the dev-push pre-push hook's cache mirroring
  (`mirror_suite_cache`, `src/doctor/hook-upgrade.ts` in ContextHub /
  `.githooks/pre-push`).
- The audit skill's F3 cache-miss path must be covered (audits running in the
  main checkout face the same race).
- Worktree creation cost is assumed negligible (node_modules is symlinked);
  latency must stay bounded.
- Implementation repo: framework skills live in the SorraAgents repo
  (`~/.pi/agent/skills` → `/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/skill`); run
  `wl` worktree-safely with `--worklog-dir` when operating there.

# Suppress known phantom test-failure patterns in triage

## Problem Statement

When the main checkout's `dev` is fast-forwarded mid-test-run by a sibling
`implement.py finish`, a suite produces failures that exist in **no single
commit** (tests from X, source from Y). The test-failure triage logic can mint
phantom `test-failure` work items from such mixed-tree output, creating noise
and false work for producers (WL-0MVSPZ1FH000RWET).

## Goal (User Story)

As a producer, I want the triage logic to detect and suppress known phantom
patterns (mixed-tree verdicts from a moving checkout) so they no longer
auto-mint critical `test-failure` work items, while genuine failures still
triage normally.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **No phantom test-failure items:** after the mitigation, the race no longer
   generates additional phantom test-failure work items without manual triage;
   existing test-failure triage logic detects and suppresses known phantom
   patterns.
2. The test-failure triage helper detects known phantom signatures — a
   `state_changed_during_run` / mid-run fast-forward flag, or output recorded
   while the executing checkout was not a stable, pinned tree — and suppresses
   auto-creation of a `test-failure` work item, recording the suppression
   reason instead.
3. A suppressed phantom is still reported in the run's output/report with an
   explicit notice (`state_changed_during_run` notice code or equivalent),
   so the information is never silently lost — it is simply not minted as a
   critical item.
4. A genuine failure on a stable checkout still creates/updates a
   `test-failure` work item exactly as before (no behaviour change for real
   failures).
5. The suppression is covered by tests (both a phantom pattern that is
   suppressed and a genuine failure that is triaged).
6. The full project test suite passes with the change.

- `skill/triage/scripts/check_or_create.py` — the triage helper

# Evaluate release budgets

## Problem statement

The host-wide dispatch budget (2 implement, 1 audit) governs how many agent panes the downtime dispatcher may spawn at once. During a release, the ship skill sets a code-freeze marker which prevents the dispatcher from spawning new implement/audit panes. However, the release process itself runs subprocesses (audit remediation via `audit_runner.py issue`, test runs via `run_tests.py`, git/gh operations) that are not recorded in the host dispatch budget ledger. There is uncertainty about whether the current code-freeze mechanism is sufficient to protect the budget, or whether a dedicated release budget slot would be clearer.

## Users

- **Operator running a release** — *"I want to know whether the release process will consume my dispatch budget or bypass it entirely."*
- **Operator managing machine capacity** — *"I want to ensure a release doesn't accidentally overload the machine with background agent work."*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Document the current code-freeze mechanism and its interaction with the dispatch budget: which tiers are skipped, which are allowed (plan/intake still run, critical prep items may dispatch), and whether the code-freeze gate prevents all implement/audit dispatches.
2. Document the release process's subprocess calls: audit remediation (`audit_runner.py`), test runs (`run_tests.py`), and git/gh operations — and confirm none of them go through the dispatcher budget gate.
3. Assess whether a "release budget" slot (consuming both implement and audit budget slots) would add value over the existing code-freeze mechanism.
4. If a release budget is recommended, produce a concrete design: what it looks like in `budget.json`, how it integrates with the ledger, and how in-progress items are handled.
5. If a release budget is NOT recommended, document why code-freeze is sufficient and what gap (if any) it leaves.
6. The evaluation conclusion (recommendation + rationale) is recorded in the work item description and any follow-up implementation work is captured as new work items rather than left implicit.
7. All related documentation is updated to reflect the findings, including the dispatcher docs and any relevant wiki entries if the evaluation produces durable guidance.
8. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (no test regressions introduced by the analysis-only deliverable).

## Impact

Operators get a clear answer on whether a release consumes the host dispatch budget or bypasses it, so they can decide whether a dedicated release budget is worth implementing rather than guessing.

## Constraints

- Scope: analysis only; no code changes required.
- Must cover both the dispatcher's code-freeze gate and the release subprocesses.
- Must reference the open item WL-0MW50EHZ6007QBPB (generalise host budget to any work item type) and assess whether a release budget would be a natural extension.
- In-progress items at release commencement must be allowed to continue; new implement/audit dispatches must be prevented until the release finishes (pausing for producer input or completing).

## Existing state

- **Host dispatch budget** (WL-0MVXWQFGV000D2AB, completed): `~/.herdr/downtime/dispatch-budget.json` ledger; default `maxImplement: 2`, `maxAudit: 1`. Enforced via `host-dispatch-budget.ts` in the dispatcher's claim→marker→spawn pipeline. Both dispatcher paths funnel through the same gate.
- **Code-freeze** (WL-0MSBU4KMA004PKSR, completed): ship skill writes `.worklog/code-freeze.json` before gating; cleared on every exit path. During freeze: audit and non-critical implement tiers are skipped; plan/intake tiers still run; critical plan_complete candidates skipped but critical idea/intake_complete still dispatch.
- **Release subprocesses**: `audit_runner.py issue <id>` runs audits as subprocesses (not dispatched panes); `run_tests.py` runs tests as subprocesses. Neither touches the budget ledger.
- **Open item** WL-0MW50EHZ6007QBPB: generalise host budget to any work item type (absent = unlimited). Currently only `implement` and `audit` kinds are budgetable; plan/intake/risk-effort are uncapped.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** The code-freeze gate (`frozen = freezeStatus === 'frozen' || freezeStatus === 'ambiguous'`) already prevents all new implement/audit dispatches during a release. If true, a dedicated release budget may be redundant.
- **Risk:** Release subprocesses (`audit_runner.py`, `run_tests.py`) run outside the dispatcher pipeline and may consume machine resources without being counted against the budget. This could be the real gap the operator is concerned about.
- **Risk (scope creep):** The evaluation may reveal that the open generalisation item (WL-0MW50EHZ6007QBPB) already covers the need; if so, record that as a related item rather than expanding this item's scope.
- **Assumption:** Plan/intake tiers are low-risk prep and are intentionally allowed during code-freeze. A release budget that blocked them too would be a behaviour change requiring explicit producer approval.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/code-freeze.ts` — code-freeze marker detection and tri-state read
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch.ts` — dispatcher code-freeze gate (line 453: `frozen = freezeStatus === 'frozen' || freezeStatus === 'ambiguous'`)
- `packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.ts` — budget ledger, config schema, live/fresh counting
- `packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.admission.ts` — generic admission, refusal tokens
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/ship/scripts/run-release.js` — release process, code-freeze write/clear
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — audit subprocess execution (budget-agnostic)
- `packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.interactive.ts` — over-quota gate for hand-fired dispatches

## Related work

- WL-0MVXWQFGV000D2AB — Host-wide concurrency budget for implement and audit dispatches (completed epic)
- WL-0MW50EHZ6007QBPB — Generalise host dispatch budget to any work item type (open, intake_complete)
- WL-0MSBU4KMA004PKSR — Code Freeze: herdr plugin blocks implement actions during ship-it process (completed)
- WL-0MW5KC8J300942EA — Stale audit dispatch-budget ledger entry survives its closed pane (completed)
- WL-0MW9X7EJ6009EL6E — Host-budget refusal early-returns from head scans, starving plan/intake behind an implement candidate (open) — closely related: shows budget refusals can abort head scans
- WL-0MTII48OV008P2QU — Global slot budget (completed) — machine-wide coordination precedent

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MW9X7EJ6009EL6E** – Host-budget refusal early-returns from head scans, starving plan/intake behind an implement candidate (open)
- **WL-0MQOIBGIR006CWLR** – Add Background Task Runtime for Non-Blocking Operations (completed)
- **WL-0MTII48OV008P2QU** – Global slot budget (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — budget, dispatch, audit, implement, release, slots
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — budget, dispatch, audit, implement, release, code-freeze
- `CLI.md` — budget, dispatch, audit, implement, release

## Evaluation conclusion

**Decision: a dedicated "release budget" slot is NOT recommended. The Code Freeze mechanism is sufficient for the window it owns.**

- **Code-freeze covers the release window for the releasing project.** While `.worklog/code-freeze.json` is `frozen` or `ambiguous` (fail-closed), the dispatcher skips every new **audit** and **implement** dispatch (critical and non-critical alike), still allows **plan/intake** prep (including critical prep), and lets **in-progress** panes finish. A freeze skip reports `code-freeze` (never `no-candidate`), so dispatch resumes immediately on the first tick after the release exits.
- **The release process bypasses the budget entirely.** `audit_runner.py`, `run_tests.py`, `git`/`gh` and `/skill:ship` itself never call `admitHostDispatch`, so a release neither consumes nor is limited by `maxImplement`/`maxAudit`. Confirmed by source inspection: no budget-ledger references in `audit_runner.py` or `run_tests.py`, and `budgetKindForAgentCommand` recognises only `/skill:implement*` and `/skill:audit*`.
- **Why no release slot:** the ledger's unit is a dispatched pane keyed by work-item id and released on pane close. Release subprocesses are not panes and have no item key; a "release" entry would be a declaration, not a measurement — it would throttle other work without bounding the release's real CPU/memory load. The release already bounds its own subprocesses (serial, budgeted audit remediation; a single test gate) and the host-CPU dispatch gate refuses new heavy work machine-wide at saturation.
- **Not an extension of WL-0MW50EHZ6007QBPB:** that item generalises caps across *dispatch kinds* (panes); a release is not a dispatch kind.
- **Residual gap (medium):** the freeze is **per worklog root** while the budget is **host-wide**, so a release in one project does not pause another project's implement/audit dispatch. Captured as follow-up **WL-0MWAM5N75004ROSW** (host-wide release barrier), which reuses the machine-coordination dir instead of a budget slot.
- **Accepted residual gap (low):** release subprocesses are invisible to the ledger; bounded by `SHIP_AUDIT_REMEDIATION_*` limits and the host-CPU gate. No follow-up required.

**Artefact:** [`docs/dev/release-dispatch-budget-evaluation.md`](docs/dev/release-dispatch-budget-evaluation.md) (tier table, subprocess inventory, full rationale). Durable guidance is cross-referenced from `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` and `packages/herdr/README.md`.

## Follow-up work

- **WL-0MWAM5N75004ROSW** — Host-wide release barrier: pause new implement/audit dispatch on every root while a release runs (closes the scope gap above).
- **WL-0MW50EHZ6007QBPB** — Generalise host dispatch budget to any work item type (related, orthogonal; no scope change).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying questions were required: the seed description was sufficient to draft a clear evaluation brief (problem, users, existing state, constraints, risks, and key files), and the surrounding work items (WL-0MVXWQFGV000D2AB budget epic, WL-0MSBU4KMA004PKSR code-freeze, WL-0MW50EHZ6007QBPB generalisation) provided the necessary context. Any design decision arising from the evaluation will be recorded here when the evaluation is executed.

## Goal

As a producer browsing the Herdr worklog selection list, I want the items that **block** a visible blocked item to also be **visible**, and in the **same group** as the blocked item, so that I can see (and dispatch) the work that must be finished before the blocked work can start — instead of seeing "blocked" rows whose blockers are nowhere in the list.

**Reported symptom (llm-proxy worklog):** `LP-0MW7V0S6A006DKZ4`, `LP-0MW7V14DN007F127` and `LP-0MVMHNUAR006SRZT` are visible in the Herdr selection list, but their blocking items are not visible anywhere in the list.

**Discovered from:** llm-proxy work items `LP-0MW7V0S6A006DKZ4` (Group 1 validation), `LP-0MW7V14DN007F127` (Group 2 validation) and `LP-0MVMHNUAR006SRZT` (Optimise llama-server prefill latency). Those ids are foreign to this store; they are listed only as evidence.

## Reproduction (measured 2026-11-08)

Selection list for the llm-proxy worklog (`/home/rgardler/projects/llm`), with `browseItemCount = 20` (`~/.config/herdr/worklog-plugin.json`):

| Visible blocked item | Stage | Active blocker(s) (status / stage / parent) |
|---|---|---|
| `LP-0MW7V0S6A006DKZ4` | intake_complete | `LP-0MW7V292T0020G02` open / intake_complete / **root**, `LP-0MW7V29MA009MCPI` open / intake_complete / **root** |
| `LP-0MW7V14DN007F127` | intake_complete | `LP-0MW7V2D13004ZO65` open / intake_complete / **root**, `LP-0MW7V2DK400365ER` open / intake_complete / **root**, `LP-0MW7V0S6A006DKZ4` (blocked — already visible) |
| `LP-0MVMHNUAR006SRZT` | plan_complete | `LP-0MVNBJWG6006Z7YQ` open / intake_complete / **child of the blocked item** |
| `LP-0MW0KZVRX005VPMT` | idea | `LP-0MW7V14DN007F127` (blocked — already visible) |

Verified by driving the **real** functions against the live data: build the pipeline input from `wl worklist -n 20 --json` (browse feed + `critical`/`reviewQueue`/`inProgressRoots`/`blockedRoots` subsets, deduped by id), then call `selectWorkItems(merged, 20)` and `regroupWorkItems(selected)` from `packages/herdr/src/`. Result: **24 rows selected — 4 `blocked` rows plus 20 `In Review` rows — and every one of the three root blockers (`LP-0MW7V292T0020G02`, `LP-0MW7V29MA009MCPI`, `LP-0MVNBJWG6006Z7YQ`) absent (HIDDEN)**. Grouping of that output: the four blocked items each sat in their own group (`Group 1`, `Group 2`, `Group 3`, `Idea`), the 20 in_review rows in `In Review`.

## Root cause 1 — the browse window is fully consumed by the mandatory review queue

1. `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` (`fetcher` wrapper) calls `fetchNextItems(clampBrowseItemCount(settings.browseItemCount))` — 20 here; the plugin default is also 20.
2. `fetchNextItems` → `assembleDefaultWorklist` / `mergeMandatoryAndSelect` (`packages/herdr/src/fetcher.root-substitution.ts`) → `selectWorkItems(merged, count)`.
3. `selectWorkItems` (`packages/herdr/src/smart-selection.ts`) always includes the mandatory set (critical ∪ `status=in-progress` ∪ `status=blocked` ∪ completed `in_review`) and then fills only `othersLimit = max(0, count − mandatory.length)` slots with everything else.
4. **A blocker is only ever an "other".** `isMandatoryItem` never matches an `open` item, and nothing in the pipeline looks at dependency edges. With 20 root completed/in_review items + 4 blocked roots in this worklog, `othersLimit = 0`, so **every** non-mandatory item is cut — including every open blocker. (This is not blocker-specific: right now the window is entirely saturated by the review queue. The blocker case is the sharpest symptom because the blockers are the items the blocked rows are waiting on.)

## Root cause 2 — no blocker→blocked grouping rule

`groupItemsByFilePaths` (`packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts`) gives **every** item with no `Key Files` section its own singleton "restricted" group. None of the items in the table above has a `Key Files` section, so even if a blocker were selected it would land in a *different* group (and its own section heading) from the blocked item it blocks. There is no rule anywhere that associates a dependency edge with group membership: edges are read only for the metadata panel's `Blocked By` rows (`fetchBlockersForItem` / `fetchOutboundDepsForItems` in `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.api.ts`).

## Root cause 3 — a child blocker is excluded by the root-only top-level rule

`LP-0MVNBJWG6006Z7YQ` is a **child of the blocked item it blocks** (`LP-0MVMHNUAR006SRZT`). `selectWorkItems` drops every item with a non-empty `parentId` (root-only top level, `WL-0MS964SIA0057ABR` / `WL-0MVN4WESM007T4XI`), so that blocker is only reachable by expanding the parent — where it does render inside the parent's group.

**The fix must keep that rule.** A blocker that is a child is never promoted to the top level; it is represented by its **ROOT ancestor** (the same parent-substitution contract the critical-child path already implements — `substituteCriticalRoots` / `walkToRootAncestor` in `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.root-substitution.ts`, `WL-0MVN4WESM007T4XI`). When the child blocker's root ancestor *is* the blocked item itself (exactly the `LP-0MVMHNUAR006SRZT` → `LP-0MVNBJWG6006Z7YQ` case) substitution collapses to an item that is already visible: nothing is added, nothing is duplicated, and the child stays reachable through expand inside the parent's group.

## Scope

**In:** the Herdr **default** worklist selection + regroup pipeline (`smart-selection.ts`, `fetcher.root-substitution.ts`, `grouping.ts`, and the blocker read they reuse); the tests named below; the doc/comment updates that state the new guarantee.

**Out:**
- **Stage-filtered views** (`fetchItemsByStage`): these are deliberately narrow, so injecting a blocker whose stage falls outside the filter would be wrong. The new guarantee is documented as default-view only.
- **Any change to the "show parents, not children" rule itself.** Children are never rendered at the top level; a child blocker is represented by its root ancestor (see Root cause 3 and AC6).
- **The `browseItemCount` policy itself** (a deep review queue starving every "other" item). If that is judged worth changing, raise it as a separate `discovered-from` item — this item only guarantees blocker visibility.
- The Pi TUI Worklog extension (its grouping copy was removed by `WL-0MSGI7PV9004UD0N`).
- `wl` core CLI grouping/scoring — the fix is Herdr-side only.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Blocker visibility (the reported defect).** For a selection list built from the current live shape (20 root completed/in_review items, 4 blocked roots, `browseItemCount = 20`), every **active** blocker of a **visible** blocked item is represented in the returned list — as the blocker itself when it is a root item, or via its root ancestor when it is a child (AC6). A test reproduces the §Reproduction shape exactly (20 in_review + 4 blocked + open blockers) in `fetcher-worklist-bundle.test.ts` against a seeded real worklog DB, and asserts each root blocker id is selected — not merely "not dropped by the count window".
- **AC2 — Same group as the blocked item.** Each pinned blocker carries the *same* `group` and `groupLabel` as the blocked item it blocks, despite having no shared key files. If a blocker blocks two or more visible blocked items that land in different groups, it appears **exactly once, in the first (lowest-numbered) group in display order**.
- **AC3 — Adjacency.** Within the group, a pinned blocker is placed immediately after the blocked item it was pinned for (deterministic: the lowest-numbered group's blocked item when it blocks several), so a blocked row is always followed by its blockers. If implementation cost forces a downgrade to "same group, anywhere in it", record that decision in a comment on this item rather than silently dropping the requirement.
- **AC4 — No duplicates, no disappearances.** The selected list contains no duplicate ids (a blocker already selected in an earlier group is not re-added), and no item that is visible today becomes invisible as a result of the change (pin-only, never remove).
- **AC5 — No-op when nothing is blocked.** When no visible item has an active blocker, the selected list and its grouping are byte-identical to today's output (regression test over a fixture with no blocked items).
- **AC6 — "Show parents, not children" preserved by parent substitution.** A blocker that is a **child** of another item is never rendered at the top level. Instead its **ROOT ancestor** (walk `parentId` to the top-most non-child item) is what gets pinned into the blocked item's group, reusing the existing `walkToRootAncestor` / `substituteCriticalRoots` machinery rather than a second implementation. Tests must cover three cases:
  - **child blocker under a third-party parent** → the root is pinned and the child id never appears at top level;
  - **child blocker whose root is the blocked item itself** (`LP-0MVMHNUAR006SRZT` / `LP-0MVNBJWG6006Z7YQ`) → no row is added at all (the substitute is already visible), no duplicate, and the child is still reachable via expand of the parent;
  - **nested child blocker** → the TOP-MOST ancestor is pinned (mirroring the existing nested-critical-child test).
  Also assert no leftover `parentId` item appears in the selected list at all (a generalisation of the existing root-only assertion), and that the existing critical-child substitution tests (`packages/herdr/src/fetcher-worklist-bundle.test.ts`) still pass unchanged.
- **AC7 — One active-blocker predicate.** Pinning uses the shared `isActiveBlocker` predicate (`packages/herdr/src/fetcher.blockers.ts`) so the pinned set can never disagree with the metadata panel's `Blocked By` rows: `completed`/`deleted` targets and targets at stage `in_review`/`done` are **not** pinned. Test covers each terminal case.
- **AC8 — Read cost.** Pinning adds **no** new `wl` process spawn per visible blocked item on the default path: reuse the in-process outbound-dep read (`fetchOutboundDepsForItems`, one batched read over all selected blocked ids) or extend the consolidated `wl worklist` bundle. State the measured spawn count before/after for the default refresh (`packages/herdr/src/fetcher-spawn-cap.test.ts` / split-guard suites stay green).
- **AC9 — Content-determinism preserved.** Group assignment remains a pure function of item content + dependency edges, never of `updatedAt`/arrival order (`WL-0MVVLBTTP003Y4XO`): the same item set and edges always produce the same pinned grouping (test: shuffle the input, assert identical group numbers).
- **AC10 — Dispatch head stated and tested.** `getHerdrListHead` derives from the same selection, so pinning changes the dispatcher's candidate ranking. Record the intended effect (blockers become dispatchable from the list head) in a comment/doc, and cover it with a test so the ordering change is deliberate rather than incidental.
- **AC11 — Docs.** Update the mandatory-subset / selection documentation (`docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md`) and the header comments of `smart-selection.ts` / `grouping.ts` to state: blockers of a visible blocked item are always shown, in the blocked item's group, first group wins, default view only.
- **AC12 — Deliberate invariant override documented.** Pinning overrides the file-path conflict invariant for the blocker/blocked pair (two conflicting items can share a group). Add the inline comment explaining why, so a later reader does not "fix" it back.

## Decisions already taken

- **"First group in the list"** means the lowest `group` integer, i.e. display order.
- **A child blocker is represented by its parent, never itself** (AC6) — the rule is "show parents, not children". The replacement is the **root ancestor** (top-most item), matching the critical-child precedent, not merely the immediate parent; promoting the child would re-introduce the duplicated-row bug that `WL-0MS964SIA0057ABR` / `WL-0MVN4WESM007T4XI` removed. Where the substituted root is the blocked item itself the pin is a no-op (no duplicate row).
- **Pinning beats file-path packing** for the blocker/blocked pair (the user requirement), documented per AC12.
- Only **direct** blockers are pinned. A pinned blocker that is itself blocked is not chased transitively unless it is already mandatory — keep the rule simple and documented; transitive closure can be a follow-up if it proves necessary.

## Key Files
- `packages/herdr/src/smart-selection.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.root-substitution.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.api.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.blockers.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/smart-selection.test.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher-worklist-bundle.test.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist-visibility.test.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/grouping.test.ts`
- `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md`

## Related

- `WL-0MV71WBHB007D8ZE` — blocked items made mandatory (the reason the blocked rows are visible while their blockers are not).
- `WL-0MV8EZRDJ001TDA8`, `WL-0MVBMLY2Z0032CYR` — `Blocked By` metadata rows (per-item only; no list membership).
- `WL-0MS964SIA0057ABR`, `WL-0MVN4WESM007T4XI` — root-only top level / critical-child root substitution (AC6 must not regress these).
- `WL-0MVVLBTTP003Y4XO` — content-deterministic group assignment (AC9).
- `WL-0MVI0HX58009JJRF` — `wl worklist` consolidated read (the natural place to add batched blocker edges if AC8 is met there).

# Audit over-subscribed dialog is incorrect

## Problem statement

The herdr selection list's over-quota confirmation dialog (shown when the operator presses `a-a` to fire `/skill:audit` while the audit tier is at/over its host cap) reports a stale/inflated audit count. The worklist header counter was recently fixed to exclude dead (pane-gone) audit entries, but the dialog still uses the old admission-count rule, so the two surfaces disagree: the header says `audit 0/1` while the dialog claims `1 running, max 1`.

## Users

- **Herdr operators** firing audits by hand from the selection list. Example user story: "As an operator who just saw `[budget: implement 0/2 · audit 0/1]` in the header, when I press `a-a` to run an audit I expect the over-quota dialog — if shown at all — to quote the same audit count I just saw, not a phantom `1 running`."

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/host-budget-dialog.ts` — renders the over-quota dialog from `HostBudgetPromptRequest { kind, live, max }`; quotes `live` verbatim ("(`<live>` running, max `<max>`) — over by `<overshoot>`").
- `packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.interactive.ts` — `prepareInteractiveAgentDispatch` decides whether to prompt. It computes the tier count via `readTierCount`, which for the audit tier calls `freshCount` (marker-compatible: every fresh entry counts, no live-pane requirement).
- `packages/herdr/src/host-budget-status.ts` — `readHostBudgetStatus` (the header counter) uses `reduceAuditDisplayCounts`, a **pane-aware** display rule: a fresh confirmed entry whose `paneId` is absent from the trusted live pane list is excluded. This was introduced by WL-0MW8D4UQH002TWJV ("Audit budget header must not count a dead (pane-gone) audit entry", completed 2026-11-09).
- `packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.ts` — `freshCount`/`reduceMarkerCounts` (admission, marker-compatible) vs `reduceAuditDisplayCounts` (display, pane-aware) are intentionally different reductions.
- Combined consequence: the **display** count and the **admission** count can differ by exactly the dead-pane entries. The interactive dialog quotes the admission count, so it reads higher than the header.

## Desired change

Make the interactive over-quota dialog quote the same audit count the operator sees in the worklist header — i.e. the pane-aware **display** count — while leaving the dispatcher's admission semantics (fail-closed, marker-compatible) untouched.

Concretely: in `prepareInteractiveAgentDispatch`'s count path for the audit tier, use the pane-aware display reduction (the same one `readHostBudgetStatus` uses) to populate both the prompt decision and the `live` value quoted in `HostBudgetPromptRequest`, so:

- a fresh audit entry whose `paneId` is absent from the trusted live pane list is **not** counted in the dialog (and does not, on its own, trigger the prompt);
- an unconfirmed audit entry (no `paneId`, reserve→spawn window) is still counted;
- an audit entry whose pane is live is still counted;
- stale entries stay excluded;
- the implement tier's counting is unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The over-quota dialog's audit `live` count matches the worklist header's audit display count for the same ledger and live pane list (the two surfaces no longer disagree).
- A dead (confirmed) audit entry whose `paneId` is absent from the live pane list does not trigger the over-quota dialog and is not quoted in it; an unconfirmed fresh audit entry and a fresh audit entry with a live pane still trigger/count; stale entries are excluded.
- Dispatcher admission (`readAuditBudgetState`/`freshCount`/`admitHostDispatch`) is unchanged: fail-closed, marker-compatible counting, 2 h staleness release.
- The implement-tier dialog behaviour and counts are unchanged.
- Unit tests pin the dialog-vs-header agreement (dead / live / unconfirmed / stale audit entries) and the unchanged admission behaviour.
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` documents that the interactive dialog's audit display count follows the header's pane-aware rule.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

Operators see the same audit count in the over-quota dialog as in the worklist header, so firing `a-a` no longer pops a phantom "1 running" prompt when no audit is actually in flight.

## Constraints

- Must not change dispatcher admission semantics (fail-closed; `maxAudit` governs dispatcher ticks).
- Must keep the display read read-only (no ledger reap/rewrite from the dialog path).
- The live pane list must remain a trusted machine-wide read; an absent list must fall back to the freshness rule (as the header does) rather than inventing a zero.
- No new dependencies; reuse existing pure reductions.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.interactive.ts` — switch the audit-tier count fed to the prompt from `freshCount` to the pane-aware display reduction (needs the live pane list it already reads).
- `packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.interactive.test.ts` — pin dialog-vs-header agreement and the dead/live/unconfirmed/stale cases.
- `packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.ts` — reuse `reduceAuditDisplayCounts` (no new reduction unless a shared helper is warranted).
- `packages/herdr/src/host-budget-status.ts` — reference for the pane-aware display rule.
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — document the dialog's display-count rule.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope-creep risk (default):** Only the dialog's audit count is changed. The dispatcher's admission logic, the header counter, and the implement tier are untouched. If further alignment is desired (e.g. implement tier using display count in the dialog), file as a separate item.
- **Count divergence trade-off:** After the change, the dialog may not prompt at all when only dead-pane entries are present — the operator can fire an audit that admission (marker-compatible) would refuse. This is intentional: the operator sees the count they saw in the header and is making an informed choice.
- **Assumption:** The live pane list is already read in `prepareInteractiveAgentDispatch` and is available for the audit-tier display count. No new subprocess calls needed.

## Related work

- **WL-0MW8D4UQH002TWJV** — "Audit budget header must not count a dead (pane-gone) audit entry" (completed): introduced the pane-aware display rule for the header. This item makes the dialog follow the same rule.
- **WL-0MW5KC8J300942EA** — parent of the above (sweep/release backstop for closed panes).
- **WL-0MVXY0Z93002HKCZ** — the F4 interactive over-quota dialog (origin of the count source this item corrects).
- **WL-0MVXWQFGV000D2AB** — parent host dispatch budget work.
- **WL-0MTOFAUCH00217XL** – "Fix: derive header count from WorkItem rows only" (completed): header-count derivation (worklist list rows, not budget). Related header-count correctness precedent.
- **WL-0MW454I1X009Q17E** – "Group counts are incorrect" (open): another selection-list count surface. Related display-count correctness.
- **WL-0MTOFANL6004M3TY** – "Test: header count excludes heading rows" (completed): test precedent for header-count correctness.

### Related docs

- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — documents the host dispatch budget, the F4 dialog and the pane-aware audit display rule.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — herdr plugin overview.
- `CLI.md` — CLI reference.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interactive questions were required — the bug and its root cause were fully resolvable from the repository and worklog.

- Q: "Which surfaces disagree, and why?" — Answer (agent, from repo research): The worklist header (`readHostBudgetStatus` → `reduceAuditDisplayCounts`, pane-aware) excludes dead confirmed audit entries; the interactive over-quota dialog (`prepareInteractiveAgentDispatch` → `readTierCount` → `freshCount`, marker-compatible) counts them. Source: `packages/herdr/src/host-budget-status.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.interactive.ts`.
- Q: "Was the header fixed recently by another item?" — Answer (agent, from worklog): Yes — WL-0MW8D4UQH002TWJV ("Audit budget header must not count a dead (pane-gone) audit entry", completed 2026-11-09) introduced the pane-aware display rule for the header only, deliberately leaving admission unchanged. Source: `wl show WL-0MW8D4UQH002TWJV`.
- Q: "Should the dialog follow the display rule or the admission rule?" — Answer (agent, from intent): The dialog is a user-facing prompt that must agree with the header the operator just read; it should quote the pane-aware display count. Admission remains marker-compatible and fail-closed. Source: item description + WL-0MW8D4UQH002TWJV design note.
- Q: "Is the live pane list already available in the interactive path?" — Answer (agent, from repo research): Yes — `prepareInteractiveAgentDispatch` already reads the machine-wide live pane list (`readLivePanes`) for the implement tier, so no new subprocess read is needed. Source: `packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.interactive.ts`.

# Herdr audit admission queries the proxy-managed budget

## Goal

Make the herdr downtime dispatcher's **audit-tier** capacity decision read the proxy's audit availability (the shared local resource) instead of asserting a per-host `budget.json` cap, so two ContextHub instances on different servers cannot independently believe they are under cap.

**discovered-from:** LP-0MW0KZUJP0019SLS (llm worklog — "Serialise audits at the shared local resource, not per host or per repo").

**Producer direction (2026-11-09):** `budget.json` is managed per ContextHub host and ContextHub may run on several servers; it is better for the proxy to manage the budget and for ContextHub to query it than for each host to enforce its own cap.

## Impact

Audit dispatch on any ContextHub host now takes its capacity decision from the proxy's shared audit budget, so a second audit is refused while one is already running anywhere — no more two concurrent audits on the one GPU — and an unreachable proxy stops audits with a named `audit-budget-unknown` reason instead of silently admitting a duplicate.

## Problem

`getActiveAudit` (`packages/herdr/src/index.ts`) reads the machine-scoped ledger (`host-dispatch-budget.ts`, `dispatch-budget.json`) and the per-host `budget.json` cap (`maxAudit`, default 1). The host-wide guard serialises audits **on one machine**, but the resource they contend for is the single local `llama-server` GPU shared by every host. Two ContextHub hosts enforcing one audit each produce two concurrent audits on one GPU — the 2026-11-03 incident. The `machine-coordination.ts` comment already records the limitation: "single-machine v1 only; multi-machine (flock/NFS) is out of scope".

The proxy already owns the audit budget and the live audit-lease registry (sibling llm item LP-0MW95FYMH006XYNK), and every ContextHub host already talks to the proxy for model traffic.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Audit admission is proxy-derived.** For the audit tier only, `getActiveAudit` / the dispatch gate queries the proxy's audit-availability endpoint (cap, live leases, available) and does not assert the local `budget.json` cap. The implement tier keeps its existing per-host budget (out of scope).
- **AC2 — One vocabulary, no disagreement.** The refusal reason token and log vocabulary match the proxy's (`audit-budget-saturated`), so a dispatcher admission and a proxy refusal cannot disagree; a divergence is logged with both sides' evidence.
- **AC3 — Fail-safe on an unreachable proxy.** If the proxy cannot be reached, audit dispatch fails **closed** with a named reason (e.g. `audit-budget-unknown`) and logs the proxy error; the legacy local-ledger path remains behind an explicit flag for one release.
- **AC4 — Single-machine limitation documented.** The `~/.herdr/downtime` single-machine constraint and the chosen cross-machine mechanism (proxy-owned budget + query) are documented, superseding the "out of scope" note in `machine-coordination.ts`.
- **AC5 — Testing/validation.** Tests cover: availability read maps to the dispatch decision; second audit refused with agreement between dispatcher and proxy; unreachable proxy fails closed; stale-lease reclamation reflected; the implement tier is unchanged. Changed-scope tests pass via `/skill:test`.
- **AC6 — Docs.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (gate table, machine-dir files, reason tokens, operator runbook), and `budget.json` is no longer documented as audit-authoritative.
- **AC7 — Full suite.** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (enforced at the dev-push gate).

## Out of scope

- The proxy-side budget/lease implementation (sibling llm item LP-0MW95FYMH006XYNK).
- Implement-tier budget changes.
- Multi-machine herdr leader election beyond audit admission.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — `getActiveAudit` audit-tier query path.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch.ts` / `downtime-worker.dispatch-filter.ts` — audit gate consumption of the proxy availability.
- `packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.ts` — legacy path behind a flag; availability vocabulary.

# herdr worklist: substituted critical-child root loses `childCount`, so the parent cannot be expanded and the critical child is unreachable

## Goal

A critical **child** work item whose root ancestor is pulled into the worklist by
critical-child root substitution must be reachable in the herdr Work Items pane:
the substituted root row must render an expand arrow and expand to show its
children, exactly as it does when the same root arrives from the browse feed.

## Problem

Observed 2026-11-12 in the live Work Items pane (`wD:p180`, worklog root
`/home/rgardler/projects/llm/.worklog`):

```
    ⭐  🔓📋✅   LP-0MW0KZUJP0019SLS Serialise audits at the shared local resource… [plan_complete] ⭐ high
```

Two leading spaces where every expandable row renders `▶`/`▼`:

```
  ▶ ⭐  ⛔📋❌   LP-0MW7V14DN007F127 …
```

`LP-0MW95FYMH006XYNK` (**Proxy owns the audit admission budget and exposes
availability**, `critical`, `open`, `intake_complete`) is a child of
`LP-0MW0KZUJP0019SLS`. The top level only renders root items
(`selectWorkItems`, `packages/herdr/src/smart-selection.ts` rootOnly gate), so
the child is only reachable by expanding its parent — and the parent cannot be
expanded, so the child never appears.

**Root cause.** `substituteCriticalRoots`
(`packages/herdr/src/fetcher.root-substitution.ts`) resolves a critical child's
ancestors through the in-process DB fast path (`db.get`) or the `wl show`
fallback (`fetchItemDetails`, `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.api.ts:306`). Neither
emits `childCount`; only the enrichments in `wl list` / `wl next` /
`wl worklist` do (e.g. the child read at `fetcher.api.ts:517`). With
`childCount === undefined` every expand path is gated off:

- `worklist.ts:271` — the arrow renders only when `childCount > 0`;
- `worklist.ts:1601` — `Tab` toggles only when `childCount > 0`;
- `worklist.ts:5329` — that `Tab` path is the only on-demand
  `fetchChildrenForItem` entry, so children are never even fetched.

**Reproduction** with the plugin's own source (no mocks), worklog root
`/home/rgardler/projects/llm/.worklog`:

```
root via substitution: present cc=undefined
critical child at top level: false
```

i.e. `mergeMandatoryAndSelect(browseWithoutRoot, allMandatory, 25,
fetchItemDetails)` returns the root with `childCount === undefined`. The same
root fetched normally carries `childCount: 9`.

**Trigger condition.** When the root does not win one of the `browseItemCount`
"other" slots (in the observed case `othersLimit = 0`: 24–25 mandatory rows in
a 25-item window), `mergeUniqueById(enrichedItems, substituted.mandatory)` has
no enriched copy to keep, and `ensureSubstitutedRoots` restores the substituted
(childCount-less) object. Whenever the root is *in* the browse window the
enriched copy wins and the arrow is correct — so the defect is window-pressure
dependent.

**Impact beyond display.** `getHerdrListHead` (`packages/herdr/src/index.ts:527`)
feeds the downtime dispatcher the same `fetchNextItems` output. The list head
therefore offers the substituted root (here: no `risk`/`effort` → a
`risk-effort` dispatch) and never the release-blocking critical child, so the
child is invisible to both the operator and auto-dispatch. The data layer is
otherwise sound: `wl next -n 25` ranks the child #1 and
`wl show LP-0MW0KZUJP0019SLS --children --json` returns it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Substituted roots are expandable.** A root injected by
  `substituteCriticalRoots` carries the same `childCount` a browse/`wl list`
  fetch would give it, so `formatItemLine` renders `▶` for it.
- **AC2 — Children are reachable.** With the root substituted (browse feed
  deliberately without it), `Tab`/`Enter` on that row triggers the on-demand
  child fetch and the critical child renders underneath it.
- **AC3 — Regression test for the window-pressure case.** A unit test asserts
  that when `othersLimit === 0` and a critical child's root is only in the
  mandatory set, the returned root has `childCount > 0` and is expandable;
  a second test pins that the browse-sourced root keeps its enriched
  `childCount` (no double-count, no clobber).
- **AC4 — Dispatcher head parity.** A test asserts the Herdr list head
  (`getHerdrListHead` / `fetchNextItems`) exposes the same expandable root
  shape used for rendering, so display and dispatch cannot diverge.
- **AC5 — Docs.** The critical-child root substitution comment block in
  `fetcher.root-substitution.ts` (and the reachability contract note in
  `smart-selection.ts`) records that substituted roots must carry
  `childCount`, and why a stripped ancestor is unsafe.
- **AC6 — Tests.** Changed-scope tests pass via `/skill:test`; the full suite
  passes at the dev-push gate.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.root-substitution.ts` — `substituteCriticalRoots`
  / `walkToRootAncestor` ancestor lookups (`db.get`, injected `itemDetails`).
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.api.ts` — `fetchItemDetails` (no `childCount`),
  `readChildrenInProcess` (already computes `db.getChildCounts(allRaw)` at
  line ~504 — the reusable source).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — expand affordances gated on `childCount`
  (lines 271, 1601, 5329).
- `packages/herdr/src/*.test.ts` — new regression tests (AC3/AC4).

## Out of scope

- The rootOnly top-level rendering rule itself (`selectWorkItems`).
- Any `llm`-side change; this is a `packages/herdr` display/reachability defect.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** `childCount` is the canonical "has children" signal for the
  expand affordance; two independent gates (`worklist.ts:1601`, `5329`) agree.
- **Risk:** counting children at ancestor-resolution time could add cost to a
  refresh. Mitigation: reuse the existing single-connection in-process
  `getChildCounts` pass rather than a per-item spawn, and fall back to leaving
  the arrow absent (today's behaviour) if the read fails — fail-open, never a
  crash.
- **Discovery:** found while investigating why `LP-0MW95FYMH006XYNK` (llm
  worklog) was absent from the herdr Work Items pane.
